title: Hosted API surge sentinel rollout and experimental idempotency shim
creator: Jordan Patel
description:
Summary:
High-severity customer escalations (multiple enterprise tenants) over the past 48h exposed a pattern of sudden 5xx/timeouts from the Hosted API correlated with tenant bursts. Symptoms: elevated 5xx rate on the hosted surface, long tail request timeouts, and increased client-side retry storms that amplified load.

What we observed (timeline):
- 2026-03-09 23:00 UTC: first tenant spike; Grafana alerted 5xx rate + latency deviation on streaming endpoints.
- 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC: initial mitigation (edge rate knobs) reduced immediate surface noise but a second wave identified a streaming connection leak in the Edge Stream Proxy (ESP) and inconsistent KV cache TTLs between proxy and runtime.
- 2026-03-10 05:30 UTC: customer escalations opened; SRE and runtime on-call engaged.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by traces and heap/dump analysis):
1) ESP connection leak causes long-lived inflight connections that hold KV cache entries and kernel resources longer than expected, causing batch backpressure on inference runtimes.
2) SDK/consumer retry logic (many customers on older SDK versions) issues aggressive immediate retries on timeouts; without per-request idempotency these retries re-enter the system and multiply inflight work.
3) Mismatch between keepalive/timeout defaults in edge vs runtime led to premature runtime-side evictions; that eviction + retry storms produced sporadic 5xx waves.

Short-term mitigations already applied:
- Deployed temporary edge admission throttles (tenant-scoped leaky bucket) to prevent immediate blast radius.
- Enabled conservative keepalive/timeouts at the frontend to favor fast-fail for clearly stalled streams.
- Communicated to impacted customers with recommended SDK config (backoff and jitter) and provided an escape hatch (tenant opt-out to dedicated fallback).

Proposed permanent fixes (this ticket):
A) Experimental idempotency shim in ESP (feature flag: retry_quarantine_v2): ESP will accept and cache idempotency tokens for a short quarantine window (60s) and silently coalesce duplicate inflight requests before fanning out to runtime. Rationale: reduce amplification at the edge without requiring immediate SDK upgrades.
B) Harmonize TTL/keepalive defaults: align ESP keepalive with runtime KV TTL to avoid premature evictions and ensure consistent resource lifetimes.
C) Patch connection leak in ESP: fix connection state machine bug that prevents connection reclaim when clients close mid-stream (PR linked below).
D) Add tenant-scoped retry-quarantine controller in frontdoor: automatic temporary 429 gating for tenants that exceed retry amplification thresholds.

Implementation plan and rollout:
- Phase 0: unit + integration tests and synthetic load (branch: feature/esp-idempotency-shim).
- Phase 1 (canary 5%): enable shim+harmonized TTL for a small ring of non-critical regions, 24h observation window, rollback kill-switch ready.
- Phase 2 (30%): expand to production non-enterprise tenants and watch tail latencies and 5xx rate.
- Phase 3 (100%): full rollout only after meeting SLOs for 72h; follow with runtime-1.21 service release that includes leak fix.

Observability and test plan:
- New Grafana panel (temp): "ESP idempotency-coalesced vs 5xx" and per-tenant replay rate (link below).
- Tracing: add span tags for idempotency_token and coalesce_decision to trace sampling.
- Load tests: run synthetic retry storms (10k qps burst profiles) against canary ring to validate coalescing behavior.

Safety and rollback:
- Feature flagging via FF platform (retry_quarantine_v2) with immediate global kill switch.
- Gradual rollout with automated SLO guardrails: if 5xx or p95 latency increase by more than 8% over baseline, auto-disable and notify on-call.

Customer comms and support:
- Drafted status updates for affected tenants and support playbook (link to Confluence).
- Provided temporary dedicated fallback instructions for customers requiring immediate isolation.

Artifacts / links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/2147 (ESP idempotency shim + leak fix)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2152 (TTL harmonization and unit tests)
- Runbook: https://redwood-infra.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RUN/pages/585/Mitigations
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-infra.com/d/hosted/5xx-spikes
- Customer issue tracker: internal ticket RED-4321 (customer-facing comms drafts)

Open questions / trade-offs we discussed:
- Coalescing at edge reduces duplicate work but may hide client retries that indicate upstream SDK bugs. We decided to default to a short quarantine window (60s) to balance correctness vs cost savings.
- Idempotency token semantics: we accept arbitrary strings but will log tokens for detection. Long-term we plan to standardize idempotency header in SDKs.
- Risk: mis-coalescing non-idempotent workloads. Mitigation: default off for write-like routes and explicit opt-in in route config.

Acceptance criteria (definition of done):
- ESP PR merged and staged behind FF; leak fix included.
- End-to-end integration tests pass in CI + synthetic load profile passes.
- Canary rollout to 5% with no SLO regressions for 24h, monitored by on-call.
- Customer-facing comms updated and support runbook validated.

Next steps (owner: Sana Kapoor):
- Complete PR reviews and get SRE sign-off (48h).
- Schedule canary rollout and coordinate with on-call (today +1).
- Run synthetic retry storm tests and capture metrics.
